digest.component_or_area: CI artifact probe, import integrity checking
propositions: CI's wheel-probe step only runs shallow imports (rebar, entry-points, JSON walk) and misses rebar subpackage import failures, scripts module sys.path contracts, and stale optional-dependency allowlists.

A two-leg deterministic import walk must cover all rebar.* modules via pkgutil.walk_packages + importlib.import_module (451 modules in base wheel) and all top-level scripts/*.py in isolated child processes to prevent sys.path.insert leaks.

Expected-optional modules (rebar._mcp_auth, rebar.opcert_service.app, rebar.review_bot.app) must be attempted and only recorded as skip when ModuleNotFoundError.name matches declared dependency and that dependency is absent.

Scripts leg must isolate each top-level script in a child process with scripts/ dir and CWD stripped from sys.path to reproduce the documented standalone contract and catch bare imports like alert_dedup.

The walk must report all import failures at once (not fail-fast) with tracebacks and exit 1 on any real failure, and be locally runnable via `python scripts/check_import_walk.py` and `make import-walk` from any dev venv without CI dependency.

Historical regressions (subpackage breakage, bare scripts imports, stale optional-dependency tables) must be caught by RED-first regression tests and validated against live base-wheel walk (0 failures, 3 skips, 451 rebar passed; 0 failures, 1 skip, 58 scripts passed).
